reviews.comment: This class was incredibly easy as long as you stay on top of the workload. Prof is great, just study in advance and don't slack and you'll be fine.
Dedicate a minimum of 1 hour a day to Zybooks, and you'll be good.

He was amazing! I had no previous coding experience and came out knowing a lot. He is very understanding and accessible. The class itself does require teamwork and individual assignments every week, and he kind of  "segregated" the groups: women together, transfer students or change of major students together, etc. It was pretty annoying.
Great teacher explains things well, lots of coursework and very long assignments for ENGR102. Choose a good team for labs and allow time for assignments.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's a pretty good professor and explains topics well. We did do some AI assignments that weren't relevant to the course. I never had any Python experience, so I would recommend genuinely doing the ZyBooks if you want to make a B or higher in the class. He curves well, but don't be too reliant on it.

He was alright. Never could really converse with him but he was very understanding about being in the corps as a fish. Just do the readings and assignments and even if you bomb the test at least you'll get a B. He curved my final course grade significantly which was much appreciated.

He is the GOAT. Very respectable and kind. He wants you to succeed and truly wants to empower his students. Keep in mind ENGR 102 at A&M is designed to be a weed-out class, so actively working and participating is something you need to do. You get what you put into the course. Good Luck, you will be fine. If you are struggling, go to Office Hours!
Great Professor, he was very helpful and communicated well. There were two influential exams, weekly Python labs, a flipped classroom style, and lots of self-learning, so prepare for those.

Great prof if you have never coded :]] He assigned the same homework as the other teachers, so you can't complain plus practice only makes you better at coding. Lectures are short and he is extremely approachable if you're confused. Only got a B since I've never coded before and was learning throughout the semester.

Plenty of homework but it really works to help you learn. Coding is best learned when applied, and that's what the hw does. My personal favorite professor this year, you can tell he cares. If you can help it, do not cheat on the labs, because those will set you up for the tests.

Mr. White is a down to earth and caring professor. He likes to keep his lectures short and lets you leave class early. He says exactly what kind of questions there will be on his quizzes and goes over similar problems in class. You can tell he wants all of his students to succeed and is always willing to help out. Definitely take him if you can 💯

Had him over the summer for an engineering preparation program, and he helped us prepare for ENGR 102. Great guy, he is very nice and caring and sometimes made goofy code examples to teach concepts. Gives good feedback.

A landfill of labs that don't feel rewarding and are only for the sake of difficulty. Exam questions are designed to waste time by adding countless extra steps that aren't seen anywhere else in the course. To much class time was spent learning how to use AI in code for no reason, as it isn't tested on.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: For engr 102 this is one of the best professors. He is very understanding of circumstances and very approachable. Any time I had a question he answered it well or pointed me to good resources. As long as you actually do the code and study a little out of the class you are good to go.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The nicest prof, I had a personal matter that really affected me and he was very understanding, and checked up, and let me make up anything i missed or needed to turn in late. He genuinely wants to see you succeed.  Very easy to reach thru email, lots of coding labs due every thursday, both in group and individual, quizzes every week

I knew Python prior to this class and it was still a nightmare. There are too many lab assignments due weekly that feel unrewarding to complete (overcomplicated and tedious for absolutely no reason), and we were forced to integrate generative AI into our programs which felt shoehorned in and a waste of time as it is not part of exams or quizzes.

As someone with prior Python experience, this class was not hard, but the amount of homework is egregious. It's mostly busy work that I didn't feel accomplished completing, more irritated by how tedious the homework labs were. I had about as much work in this class every week as my other classes combined, usually 4-7 labs due every week.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took a risk a few semesters ago taking this prof, since he didn't have a RMP back then, but ended up making the right decision. No-nonsense lectures. You can tell he is experienced. Very responsive and curved during my semester, keep up with the programming assignment and pay attention to zybooks for an easy-ish A.
Cares about student success.

One thing: if you haven't coded 102 sucks. A lot. There's nothing you can do to get around that. Before this semester I had never coded, but thanks to Prof. White, I was able to pass. He is caring, gives extra credit, and goes out of his way to check in on you. Boring lectures, but going to to class and actually doing your labs, you will succeed.

Great guy, he teaches python quite well and is very reasonable. Occasionally he goes on rants about politics or some other unrelated stuff but he would still be able to finish the content for that week. Try and get a good group since you get stuck with the same group all semester long for every python lab.

Asked him for a rec letter for applying to honors, and took time out of his saturday to chat with me about it so he could write a really good letter. Overall very caring, offers lots of extra credit, and very willing to help you succeed.

Dr. White is a really good professor. Email him about issues you're having and he'll invest in you to do well in the class. The topic about python sucks if you're new (like me), but it is something you'll just have to get use to. TAKE ADVANTAGE OF HIS EXTRA CREDIT. Those points will be the make or break between one letter grade up or down.

Professor White is a great professor that I recommend. The class is hard and anyone who hasn't coded in python before will struggle, but that's not on the teacher. Professor White clearly goes over the slides and explained things in detail, just the hardest part of the class is paying attention.

Really good professor with not a lot of work to do. Not strict on late work and also very easy to communicate with. The tests aren't too difficult if you prepare for them even though the average is usually low. Lot's of extra credit and don't get behind on your work or else exam can get tricky.

ENGR-102 is just a class designed to lower the GPA of a lot of students for ETAM, the class is very easy except for the two exams, which both had averages between 50-65 for most classes. Professor white is a good lecturer and does highlight what's important though.

Professor White's strengths were his kindness and willingness to listen to students. When people were struggling with quizzes, he started giving tips and hints before each quiz to help us out. It was his first year teaching, so lectures were just decent. Healthy curve at the end of the semester. Overall a good choice for 102.

If you don't know how to code going into this class, you will struggle. This class goes extremely fast and you have to put in loads of work for the exams, apparently. I studied for a week or two before the exams and still ended up failing both of them. Your grade will be heavily cushioned by your "labs" and group "labs" as well as weekly quizzes.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things
